messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into French, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE French line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Ah comme il est difficile de dire ce que c'était cette forêt sauvage et âpre et dense qui dans la pensée renoue la peur!

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table (Step 3)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (French) | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|------------------------------|------------------------|--------| | Ahi | exclamatory “Ah!” | Ah | Ah! | OK | | quanto | intensifier “how” (degree) | comme | how | OK | | a | infinitive marker “to” | de | to | OK | | dir | verb “to tell” | dire | to tell | OK | | qual | interrogative “what” | ce | what | OK | | era | imperfect “was” (past state) | c'était | was | OK | | è | present “is” (copula) | est | is | OK | | cosa | abstract “thing” (subject of difficulty) | c’ (in *c’est difficile*) | thing / it | **UNNECESSARY** (the noun is not expressed in French) | | dura | adjective “hard / difficult” | difficile | hard / difficult | OK | | esta | demonstrative “this” | cette | this | OK | | selva | noun “forest / wood” | forêt | forest / wood | OK | | selvaggia | adjective “wild” | sauvage | wild | OK | | e (1) | coordinating “and” | et | and | OK | | aspra | adjective “rough” | âpre | rough | OK | | e (2) | coordinating “and” | et | and | OK | | forte | adjective “strong / dense” | dense | dense | OK | | che | relative pronoun “which” | qui | which | OK | | nel | preposition+article “in the” | dans la | in the | OK | | pensier | noun “thought” | pensée | thought | OK | | rinova | verb “renews” | renoue | renews | OK | | la | definite article “the” (feminine) | la | the | OK | | paura | noun “fear” | peur | fear | OK |
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: *cosa* – the Italian noun “thing” is not lexicalised in the French rendering; French uses the dummy pronoun *c’* in *c’est difficile* instead. No other tokens are missing, wrong, or grammatically mismatched.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only French script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final French text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 4: - Original: Ah comme il est difficile de dire ce que c'était - Issue: **GRAMMAR** – “ce que c'était” is unidiomatic in French. - Corrected: Ah comme il est difficile de dire ce qu’il était - Line 5: - Original: cette forêt sauvage et âpre et dense - Issue: none - Corrected: no change - Line 6: - Original: qui dans la pensée renoue la peur! - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
```text Ah comme il est difficile de dire ce qu’il était cette forêt sauvage et âpre et dense qui dans la pensée renoue la peur! ```
